135.ev: Identifies parallel lines from their equations
135.q: If {{name}} has the line y = 3x − 2, can they write a line that's parallel to it and one that's perpendicular to it?

136.desc: Explain why the x-coordinates where y = f(x) and y = g(x) intersect solve f(x) = g(x), and find approximate solutions using graphs, tables or technology for linear, quadratic and exponential functions
136.ev: Finds approximate solutions of x² = x + 3 from graphs
136.q: If {{name}} wants to know when 2ˣ overtakes 3x + 1, can they use graphs or a table to find roughly where?

137.desc: Form and solve quadratic equations from contexts such as area and projectile height, rejecting solutions that don't make sense
137.ev: Forms a quadratic from an area problem
137.q: If {{name}} is told a rectangle's length is 3 cm more than its width and its area is 40 cm², can they form and solve a quadratic and reject the answer that doesn't make sense?

138.desc: Solve exponential equations by writing both sides with the same base (e.g. 2ˣ = 32, 9ˣ = 27) or by using tables, graphs or trial and improvement
138.q: If {{name}} wants to know how many years until £100 growing at 10% a year doubles, can they set up 1.1ˣ = 2 and find x approximately?

139.desc: Build a simple iterative model in a spreadsheet or short program where each row updates from the previous one (e.g. new balance = old balance × 1.03, new velocity = old velocity + a × Δt) and compare it with real data
139.ev: Sets up a recursive update rule in a spreadsheet
139.q: If {{name}} sets up a spreadsheet where each row is one second of a falling ball, can they write the rule that updates its speed and see how air resistance changes the result?

140.desc: Graph systems of linear inequalities to find the feasible region, and interpret points in the region as viable solutions to a constraint problem
140.ev: Shades the region satisfying two or more inequalities
140.q: If {{name}} has at most 10 hours to split between two jobs and needs to earn at least £80, can they graph the possibilities and pick a workable plan?

141.desc: Use the discriminant b² − 4ac to decide whether a quadratic has two, one or no real solutions, and connect this to how many times the parabola meets the x-axis
141.q: If {{name}} works out b² − 4ac for x² + 2x + 5 and gets a negative number, can they explain what that means for the graph?

142.desc: Carry out the full modelling cycle: identify variables and assumptions, formulate a model, compute, interpret results in context, validate against reality and revise the model
142.ev: States the assumptions behind a model
142.q: If {{name}} builds a model for how long a phone battery lasts, can they explain the assumptions they made and how they'd check and improve it?

108.desc: Use the quadratic formula x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac)) / 2a to solve any quadratic equation, giving exact (surd) or decimal answers, and know it comes from completing the square
108.ev: Identifies a, b and c correctly, including signs
108.q: If {{name}} needs to solve 2x² + 3x − 4 = 0, can they use the quadratic formula carefully and get both answers?

144.desc: Identify the effect on a graph of replacing f(x) by f(x) + k, f(x + k), k·f(x) and f(kx), and use transformations to write equations for shifted graphs
144.ev: Describes the shift caused by f(x) + 3 and f(x − 2)
144.q: If {{name}} knows the graph of y = x², can they sketch y = (x − 3)² + 1 and describe how it moved?

145.desc: Write a quadratic in vertex form y = a(x − h)² + k, read off the turning point and axis of symmetry, and use it to find maximum or minimum values in context
145.q: If {{name}} sees y = −2(x − 3)² + 8, can they say where the top of the curve is and what its maximum value is?

147.desc: Use the first few terms of a binomial expansion to approximate values such as 1.02¹⁰ and judge the accuracy of the approximation
147.q: If {{name}} needs 0.98⁶ to 4 decimal places without a calculator, can they use a binomial expansion?

146.desc: Expand (a + b)ⁿ for a positive integer n using binomial coefficients, including expressions such as (2 − 3x)⁵
146.q: If {{name}} needs to expand (2x + 1)⁶, can they do it without multiplying out six brackets?

149.desc: Extend the number system with i (i² = −1) to solve quadratics with negative discriminants, writing complex solutions in the form a ± bi
149.q: If {{name}} solves x² + 4 = 0, can they explain what the solutions are now that 'no real solution' isn't the end of the story?

152.desc: Decide whether a sequence converges to a limit or diverges, find simple limits such as (n + 1)/n → 1, and find the limit of a convergent recurrence
152.ev: Finds the limit of a sequence given by a formula
152.q: If {{name}} sees the sequence 1/2, 2/3, 3/4, …, can they say what it approaches and justify it?

153.desc: Divide a polynomial by a linear factor (by long division or inspection) and use the remainder theorem: the remainder on dividing p(x) by (x − a) is p(a), so (x − a) is a factor exactly when p(a) = 0
153.q: If {{name}} is given p(x) = x³ − 6x² + 11x − 6, can they test whether (x − 1) is a factor without dividing?

154.desc: Use the general term ⁿCᵣ aⁿ⁻ʳ bʳ to find a particular coefficient, including the term independent of x in expansions such as (x + 2/x)⁸
154.ev: Finds the coefficient of x³ in (1 + 2x)¹⁰
154.q: If {{name}} needs only the x⁴ term in (3 − x)⁹, can they find it without the full expansion?

150.desc: Describe sequences as increasing, decreasing or periodic, and justify the description from the rule
150.ev: Shows a sequence is increasing using uₙ₊₁ − uₙ
150.q: If {{name}} has the rule uₙ₊₁ = 1/uₙ with u₁ = 2, can they describe how the sequence behaves?

156.desc: Test whether data follow a suspected non-linear relationship by plotting a transformed variable (e.g. y against x² or against 1/x) and checking for a straight line through the origin
156.ev: Chooses what to plot to test y ∝ x²
156.q: If {{name}} suspects a pendulum's period squared is proportional to its length, can they say what graph to plot to check?

157.desc: Understand logarithms as the inverse of exponential functions (log_b(x) = y means bʸ = x), and use them to solve exponential equations such as a·bᶜᵗ = d
157.ev: Converts between exponential and logarithmic form
157.q: If {{name}} needs to know exactly when a population growing by 3% a year doubles, can they set it up and solve with logarithms?

160.desc: Split and combine sums, take out constant factors, change the starting index, and use Σr = n(n + 1)/2 to evaluate sums
160.q: If {{name}} needs Σ(4r − 1) from r = 11 to 30, can they evaluate it by splitting the sum?

163.desc: Use geometric series to model savings, loan repayments and repeated drug doses, including the long-term level approached when there is a sum to infinity
163.ev: Models monthly savings with a geometric series
163.q: If {{name}} takes a 100 mg dose daily and 30% remains the next day, can they find the level it settles at?

164.desc: Use quadratic functions to model situations such as projectile height, area optimisation and revenue, finding and interpreting maximum or minimum values and roots
164.ev: Builds a quadratic model for an area-maximising problem
164.q: If {{name}} has 20 m of fencing to make a rectangular pen, can they model the area with a quadratic and find the biggest possible pen?

166.desc: Classify functions as even (f(−x) = f(x), symmetric about the y-axis) or odd (f(−x) = −f(x), unchanged by a half-turn about the origin), algebraically and from graphs
166.ev: Tests f(−x) algebraically for a polynomial
166.q: If {{name}} is given f(x) = x³ − 4x and g(x) = x⁴ + 1, can they decide which is odd and which is even and explain how the graphs show it?

167.desc: Split a rational expression with linear factors in the denominator (including a repeated factor) into partial fractions by substitution or equating coefficients
167.q: If {{name}} needs to integrate or expand 3/((x − 1)(x + 2)), can they first split it into partial fractions?

168.desc: Treat a series as the sequence of its partial sums Sₙ, and say a series converges when the partial sums approach a limit
168.ev: Calculates partial sums of a series
168.q: If {{name}} adds 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/8 + …, can they use partial sums to explain why the total approaches 1?

148.desc: Build Pascal's triangle, link its entries to ⁿCᵣ, and use its patterns and symmetry
148.q: If {{name}} builds Pascal's triangle, can they explain why the numbers match the counts of combinations?

170.desc: Prove that two expressions are identically equal by manipulating one side into the other, and use identities to explain number facts (e.g. the product of two consecutive odd numbers is one less than a multiple of 4)
170.ev: Proves an identity by expanding and simplifying
170.q: If {{name}} is asked to prove that the sum of three consecutive whole numbers is always a multiple of 3, can they write an algebraic proof?

171.desc: Solve simple equations involving square roots or algebraic fractions, and explain how extraneous solutions can arise and must be checked
171.ev: Solves √(x + 3) = x − 3 and rejects an extraneous root
171.q: If {{name}} solves √x = x − 2 and gets two answers, can they check which one actually works and explain why the other appeared?

173.desc: Write recurring decimals as geometric series and use the sum to infinity to convert them to fractions
173.q: If {{name}} is told 0.999… equals 1, can they use a geometric series to explain why?

174.desc: Calculate and plot residuals (observed − predicted) to judge whether a linear model is appropriate, and use technology to compute and interpret the correlation coefficient
174.q: If {{name}} sees a residual plot shaped like a U, can they explain what that says about using a straight line for the data?

175.desc: Use exponent laws to rewrite exponential expressions to reveal different rates — e.g. 1.15ᵗ ≈ 1.012^(12t) shows a 15% annual rate as about 1.2% monthly
175.ev: Converts an annual growth factor to a monthly one
175.q: If {{name}} knows a population grows by 20% each year, can they work out roughly what the monthly growth rate is?

158.desc: Read, write and evaluate sums in sigma notation, identifying the general term and the limits of summation
158.q: If {{name}} sees Σ (2r + 1) from r = 1 to 10, can they explain what it means and evaluate it?

176.desc: Solve a system of one linear and one quadratic equation algebraically by substitution and graphically by intersection, interpreting 0, 1 or 2 solutions
176.ev: Substitutes a linear equation into a quadratic
176.q: If {{name}} wants to know where the line y = x + 1 meets the curve y = x² − 1, can they solve it algebraically and check on a graph?

177.desc: Solve quadratic inequalities such as x² − x − 6 < 0 by finding the roots and using a sketch of the parabola to choose the correct region
177.ev: Finds critical values from the roots
177.q: If {{name}} solves x² − 9 > 0, can they use a sketch to explain why the answer has two separate parts?

155.desc: Recognise and use relationships where one quantity is proportional to the square or inverse square of another (y = kx², y = k/x²), predicting the effect of doubling or halving the input
155.ev: Predicts that doubling x quadruples y when y ∝ x²
155.q: If {{name}} is told light intensity follows an inverse-square law, can they predict how bright a lamp looks from twice as far away?

161.desc: Derive the formula for the sum of a finite geometric series by multiplying by r and subtracting, and use it in contexts such as mortgage or savings payments
161.q: If {{name}} saves £1 then doubles the amount each day, can they work out the total saved after 20 days without adding every term?

159.desc: Derive and use the formula for the sum of the first n terms of an arithmetic series, Sₙ = n/2 (first + last), using Gauss's pairing idea
159.q: If {{name}} is asked to add up all the numbers from 1 to 100 quickly, can they explain the pairing trick and turn it into a formula?

162.desc: Use S∞ = a/(1 − r) for a geometric series with |r| < 1, explaining why the series diverges otherwise
162.q: If {{name}} bounces a ball that rises to 60% of its previous height each time, can they find the total distance travelled?

178.desc: Solve systems of three linear equations in three unknowns by elimination, and interpret the solution as the meeting point of three planes
178.ev: Reduces a 3×3 system to a 2×2 system
178.q: If {{name}} is given three equations about the prices of three different fruits, can they eliminate step by step to find each price?

179.desc: Identify the zeros of a factorised polynomial and use them, with the leading term, to sketch a rough graph of the function
179.q: If {{name}} sees y = (x + 1)(x − 2)(x − 3), can they sketch roughly what the graph looks like without plotting points?

180.desc: Expand (1 + x)ⁿ for negative and fractional n as an infinite series valid for |x| < 1, including (a + bx)ⁿ and expressions split into partial fractions
180.ev: Expands (1 + x)⁻¹ and recognises a geometric series
180.q: If {{name}} expands (1 − 2x)^(−1/2), can they find the first four terms and say for which x it is valid?

184.desc: Compare hyperbolic and circular functions: (cos t, sin t) traces the unit circle while (cosh t, sinh t) traces the right branch of x² − y² = 1, and the exponential definitions mirror Euler's formula
184.ev: Explains why the functions are called hyperbolic
184.q: If {{name}} is asked why sinh and cosh are called hyperbolic functions, can they link them to a hyperbola as sin and cos are linked to a circle?

186.desc: Find exact values such as cosh(ln 3) = 5/3 by substituting into the exponential definitions and using e^(ln a) = a
186.q: If {{name}} is asked for the exact value of tanh(ln 4), can they find it as a fraction?

187.desc: Sketch the graphs of sinh x, cosh x and tanh x, identifying the minimum of cosh at (0, 1), the asymptotes y = ±1 of tanh, and that cosh is even while sinh and tanh are odd
187.ev: Sketches all three graphs on axes
187.q: If {{name}} sketches y = cosh x and y = sinh x on the same axes, can they explain why the graphs get closer as x increases?

185.desc: Define sinh x = (eˣ − e⁻ˣ)/2, cosh x = (eˣ + e⁻ˣ)/2 and tanh x = sinh x / cosh x, and evaluate them with a calculator
185.ev: States the exponential definitions of sinh, cosh and tanh
185.q: If {{name}} is asked what cosh x means, can they write its definition in terms of eˣ and find cosh 0?

181.desc: Prove and use hyperbolic identities from the exponential definitions, including cosh²x − sinh²x = 1, sinh 2x = 2 sinh x cosh x and cosh 2x = cosh²x + sinh²x
181.ev: Proves cosh²x − sinh²x = 1 from the definitions
181.q: If {{name}} is asked to prove that cosh 2x = 1 + 2 sinh²x, can they do it from the exponential definitions?

190.desc: Define arsinh x, arcosh x (for x ≥ 1, taking the non-negative value) and artanh x (for |x| < 1), and sketch their graphs as reflections of the hyperbolic graphs in y = x
190.ev: Explains why cosh must be restricted to have an inverse
190.q: If {{name}} is asked why arcosh 0.5 does not exist, can they explain using the graph of cosh x?

192.desc: Derive and use arsinh x = ln(x + √(x² + 1)), arcosh x = ln(x + √(x² − 1)) and artanh x = ½ ln((1 + x)/(1 − x)) by solving a quadratic in eʸ
192.ev: Derives the logarithmic form of arsinh x
192.q: If {{name}} is asked to show that arsinh x = ln(x + √(x² + 1)), can they derive it from x = sinh y?

195.desc: Model motion such as projectiles with parametric equations in time, and interpret the parameter, domain and features of the curve in context
195.ev: Writes parametric equations for a projectile
195.q: If {{name}} models a ball thrown at 20 m/s at 30°, can they write parametric equations and find its range?

197.desc: Use Osborn's rule to turn a trigonometric identity into the corresponding hyperbolic identity by changing the sign of every product (or implied product) of two sines, and check the result from the definitions
197.ev: Applies Osborn's rule to cos 2x = 1 − 2 sin²x
197.q: If {{name}} knows sin(A + B) = sin A cos B + cos A sin B, can they write down the hyperbolic version and check it?

193.desc: Describe curves with parametric equations x = f(t), y = g(t), plot them, and convert to Cartesian form by eliminating the parameter, including circles x = r cos t, y = r sin t
193.ev: Plots a curve from a table of t values
193.q: If {{name}} is given x = 2t, y = t², can they sketch the curve and find its Cartesian equation?

198.desc: Prove statements about all positive integers, such as series formulae, by induction: a base case, an inductive step assuming the result for n = k, and a conclusion
198.q: If {{name}} is asked to prove a sum formula for all n, can they write a complete proof by induction?

199.desc: Define sech x, cosech x and coth x as the reciprocals of cosh, sinh and tanh, sketch their graphs and use 1 − tanh²x = sech²x
199.q: If {{name}} is given cosh x = 5/4, can they find the exact values of sech x and tanh x?

191.desc: Solve equations such as 3 sinh x + cosh x = 3 by rewriting in terms of eˣ to get a quadratic in eˣ, or by using an identity to get a quadratic in one hyperbolic function, rejecting impossible values
191.ev: Forms a quadratic in eˣ from a hyperbolic equation
191.q: If {{name}} needs to solve 2 cosh x − sinh x = 2, can they find all solutions in exact logarithmic form?

200.desc: Use the formulae for Σr² and Σr³ together with Σr to find sums of polynomial expressions in r
200.ev: Uses Σr² to sum the first 20 squares
200.q: If {{name}} needs the sum 1×2 + 2×3 + … + n(n + 1), can they find a formula using standard sums?

201.desc: Sum series whose terms can be written as differences, such as 1/(r(r + 1)) = 1/r − 1/(r + 1), so that most terms cancel
201.ev: Writes a general term as a difference
201.q: If {{name}} needs Σ 1/(r(r + 1)) from 1 to n, can they use partial fractions to make the terms cancel?

202.desc: Model a hanging chain or cable with the catenary y = a cosh(x/a), compare it with a parabola, and interpret the parameter a
202.ev: Recognises a catenary in hanging cables and arches
202.q: If {{name}} photographs a hanging chain, can they explain why a cosh curve models it better than a parabola?

203.desc: Show that the harmonic series 1 + 1/2 + 1/3 + … diverges by grouping terms, even though its terms tend to zero
203.ev: Groups terms to show each group exceeds 1/2
203.q: If {{name}} is told the terms of 1 + 1/2 + 1/3 + … get smaller and smaller, can they explain why the sum still grows forever?

probes.q: If {{name}} knows two angles of a triangle are 50° and 70°, can they work out the third? And can they figure out the angles inside a regular pentagon?
If {{name}} knows a ladder is 5 metres long and leans against a wall at 70° to the ground, can they use trigonometry to work out how high up the wall it reaches?
If {{name}} sees a point on the unit circle at 210°, can they say what its coordinates tell them about sin 210° and cos 210°?

143.desc: Represent and carry out geometric transformations on squared paper or a coordinate grid: reflections (in horizontal, vertical, and diagonal mirror lines, including the axes), translations (described as a vector or as left/right/up/down moves), and rotations (90° or 180° about a stated centre point); describe each transformation precisely using the correct language; identify which transformation maps one shape onto its image by comparing position, orientation, and size
143.ev: Reflect a shape in a given mirror line on a grid and label the new coordinates
143.q: If {{name}} sees a shape and its mirror image on squared paper, can they draw in the exact mirror line, and describe the reflection precisely — including where the line of reflection is — without just saying 'it flipped'?

312.desc: Use and interpret standard geometric diagram conventions: mark right angles with a small square, equal lengths with single or double tick marks, and equal angles with arc marks; label angles in three-letter notation (∠ABC) and individual angles with a single letter or number; draw diagrams showing angles at a point, angles on a straight line, and angles inside polygons with these conventions; read diagrams with these marks to identify given information and find unknown values
312.ev: Mark a right angle with a small square symbol in a diagram and explain what it means
312.q: If {{name}}'s maths diagram shows a small square in one corner and matching arc marks on two other angles, can they tell you what each mark means — and use them to figure out a missing angle without re-measuring?

362.desc: Use the properties of faces, surfaces, edges, and vertices of 3-D shapes (cubes, cuboids, prisms, cylinders, pyramids, cones, and spheres) to solve problems, including visualising cross-sections
362.ev: Count and describe the faces, edges, and vertices of a triangular prism and a square-based pyramid
362.q: If {{name}} slices a cylinder straight across the middle like cutting a tin of beans in half, can they describe the shape of the cut surface? What about slicing at an angle?

365.desc: Derive and use the angle sum in a triangle (180°), use it to deduce the angle sum in any polygon ((n−2) × 180°), and calculate interior and exterior angles of regular polygons
365.ev: Calculate a missing angle in a triangle by subtracting the known angles from 180°
365.q: If {{name}} knows two angles of a triangle are 50° and 70°, can they work out the third? And can they figure out the angles inside a regular pentagon?

369.desc: Derive and apply formulae for the area of triangles, parallelograms, and trapezia, and for the volume of cuboids and other prisms (including cylinders), connecting each formula to its geometric reasoning
369.ev: Calculate the area of a trapezium using A = ½(a + b) × h and explain why the formula works
369.q: If {{name}} needs to tile a triangular section of a patio with a base of 4 m and height of 3 m, can they work out the area to know how many tiles to buy?

371.desc: Identify properties of translations, rotations, and reflections; describe and perform these transformations on given figures, and understand that the image is congruent to the original
371.ev: Reflect a shape in a given mirror line (including diagonal lines) and state the coordinates of the image
371.q: If {{name}} is asked to rotate a triangle 90° clockwise around a fixed point, can they work out where each corner ends up — and confirm the triangle is still the same size and shape?

374.desc: Draw and measure line segments and angles accurately using ruler and protractor, and interpret scale drawings to extract real measurements
374.ev: Draw a triangle accurately given two sides and the included angle (SAS)
374.q: If {{name}} is given an architect's floor plan where 1 cm represents 2 m, can they measure a room on the plan and work out its real-world dimensions?

377.desc: Derive and illustrate properties of triangles, quadrilaterals, and circles using appropriate language, including interior angles, diagonals, symmetry, and relationships between side lengths
377.ev: List and verify properties of a parallelogram (opposite sides parallel/equal, opposite angles equal, diagonals bisect each other)
377.q: If you ask {{name}} why the diagonals of a rectangle are always equal in length, can they explain it using the properties of the shape — rather than just measuring to check?

376.desc: Use conventional geometric terms and notation to describe, sketch, and draw points, lines, parallel and perpendicular lines, right angles, regular polygons, and reflectively/rotationally symmetric polygons
376.ev: Use correct notation for line segments (AB), angles (∠ABC), and parallel lines (AB ∥ CD)
376.q: If you ask {{name}} to describe a triangle using proper geometry notation — naming its angles and sides with letters — can they do it clearly enough for someone else to draw it?

364.desc: Apply the properties of angles at a point (360°), on a straight line (180°), and vertically opposite angles to find unknown angles in multi-step problems
364.ev: Find a missing angle using the fact that angles on a straight line sum to 180°
364.q: If {{name}} is given a diagram with several angles marked at crossing lines and some unknown, can they use the rules about straight lines and crossing lines to find all the missing angles step by step?

381.desc: Know and use the criteria for triangle congruence (SSS, SAS, ASA, RHS), use standard labelling conventions for sides and angles of triangle ABC, and determine whether two triangles are congruent
381.ev: State which congruence criterion (SSS, SAS, ASA, or RHS) applies to a given pair of triangles
381.q: If {{name}} is shown two triangles where all three sides of one match all three sides of the other, can they explain why those triangles must be identical in shape and size?

382.desc: Understand and use the relationship between parallel lines cut by a transversal: corresponding angles, alternate interior angles, and co-interior (same-side interior) angles; use these to find unknown angles
382.ev: Identify alternate, corresponding, and co-interior angle pairs in a diagram with parallel lines
382.q: If {{name}} sees a Z-shape or F-shape formed by two parallel lines and a crossing line in a diagram, can they identify the equal angles and explain why they’re equal?

384.desc: Calculate the circumference and area of circles using the formulae C = πd (or 2πr) and A = πr², and solve problems involving perimeters and areas of composite shapes that include circular parts
384.ev: Calculate the circumference and area of a circle given its radius or diameter
384.q: If {{name}} wants to know how far a bicycle wheel travels in one full rotation, can they use the diameter of the wheel and π (pi) to work out the circumference?

387.desc: Understand similarity as a relationship where one shape is an enlargement of another; construct similar shapes by enlargement with a given scale factor and centre, with and without coordinate grids
387.ev: Enlarge a shape by a given scale factor from a specified centre of enlargement
387.q: If {{name}} wants to enlarge a photo so it's three times bigger, can they work out the new dimensions — and explain that the shape stays the same but all lengths increase by the same factor?

388.desc: Solve multi-step angle problems by chaining angle facts (on a line, at a point, vertically opposite, parallel lines, triangle sum), stating the geometric reason for every step
388.ev: Finds an unknown angle in a diagram with parallel lines and a triangle
388.q: If {{name}} finds a missing angle in a diagram with parallel lines, can they write down the geometric reason for every step?

389.desc: Use ruler and compasses to perform standard constructions: perpendicular bisector of a line segment, perpendicular to a line from or at a given point, and bisecting an angle
389.ev: Construct the perpendicular bisector of a line segment using compasses and a straight edge
389.q: If {{name}} has only a ruler and a pair of compasses, can they construct a line that cuts another line segment exactly in half at a right angle — without using a protractor?

390.desc: Measure, draw and calculate three-figure bearings, including back bearings found with parallel-line angle facts
390.ev: Measures a bearing on a map
390.q: If {{name}} knows a boat sails on a bearing of 070° from A to B, can they find the bearing of A from B?

391.desc: Identify and use the vocabulary of circles beyond radius and diameter: chord, arc (minor and major), sector, segment, tangent
391.ev: Labels each part on a diagram
391.q: If {{name}} is shown a slice of pizza and the piece cut off by a straight line, can they name each correctly?

393.desc: Calculate the surface area of prisms and cylinders from nets, including the curved surface of a cylinder
393.ev: Draws the net of a cylinder and labels its dimensions
393.q: If {{name}} wants to make a label for a can 12 cm tall and 7 cm across, can they work out the label's area?

395.desc: Use the trigonometric ratios sin, cos, and tan in right-angled triangles to find unknown sides and angles, including setting up the correct ratio for a given problem
395.ev: Identify which trigonometric ratio to use (SOH CAH TOA) based on the known and unknown sides
395.q: If {{name}} knows a ladder is 5 metres long and leans against a wall at 70° to the ground, can they use trigonometry to work out how high up the wall it reaches?

394.desc: Apply Pythagoras’ Theorem (a² + b² = c²) to calculate unknown side lengths in right-angled triangles, including in real-world and coordinate-geometry contexts
394.ev: Calculate the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle given the two shorter sides
394.q: If {{name}} wants to check whether a shelf bracket makes a perfect right angle and the sides measure 30 cm, 40 cm, and 50 cm, can they use Pythagoras to verify?

396.desc: Solve real-world problems with right-triangle trigonometry and Pythagoras, including angles of elevation and depression, choosing the correct ratio
396.ev: Finds the height of a building from an angle of elevation
396.q: If {{name}} stands 50 m from a tree and measures an angle of elevation of 32°, can they work out the tree's height?

398.desc: Calculate arc lengths and sector areas as fractions of the circumference and area of a circle, and solve problems involving composite shapes
398.ev: Calculates the arc length for a 72° sector
398.q: If {{name}} has a pizza slice with a 45° angle from a 30 cm pizza, can they find the length of its crust?

400.desc: Represent vectors as column vectors and directed line segments, and add, subtract and multiply vectors by scalars, linking to translations
400.ev: Adds two column vectors and draws the result
400.q: If {{name}} walks 3 right and 2 up, then 1 right and 5 down, can they write the overall journey as one column vector?

401.desc: Distinguish checking examples from proving, disprove false conjectures with a single counterexample, and explain why a general argument is needed
401.ev: Finds a counterexample to a false geometric claim
401.q: If {{name}} hears that 'any quadrilateral with equal sides is a square', can they disprove it with one example?

402.desc: Find the centre and angle of a rotation and the centre and scale factor of an enlargement from an object and its image, using construction and coordinates
402.ev: Finds a centre of rotation using perpendicular bisectors
402.q: If {{name}} is given a shape and its rotated image, can they find the centre of rotation?

403.desc: Enlarge shapes using fractional scale factors (making them smaller) and negative scale factors (image on the opposite side of the centre, inverted)
403.ev: Enlarges a shape by scale factor ½
403.q: If {{name}} enlarges a triangle by scale factor −1 about the origin, can they predict where it ends up?

404.desc: Find missing lengths in similar triangles and shapes, including overlapping triangles, by finding a scale factor or setting up a proportion
404.ev: Finds a missing side using a scale factor
404.q: If {{name}} has a smaller triangle inside a larger one with a parallel side, can they find a missing length?

405.desc: Construct loci of points a fixed distance from a point or line, equidistant from two points or two lines, and shade regions that satisfy several conditions
405.ev: Draws the locus of points 3 cm from a line segment
405.q: If {{name}} must place a mast within 4 km of a town and equally far from two roads, can they use loci to find the possible positions?

407.desc: Find the midpoint of a segment and the point that divides it in a given ratio using coordinates
407.ev: Finds the midpoint of a segment
407.q: If {{name}} has points A(1, 2) and B(11, 7), can they find the point two-fifths of the way from A to B?

408.desc: Calculate perimeters and areas of polygons from vertex coordinates using the distance formula and decomposition
408.ev: Finds the perimeter of a triangle from its vertices
408.q: If {{name}} is given the coordinates of a field's four corners, can they find its perimeter and area?

409.desc: State precise definitions of angle, circle, perpendicular and parallel lines and line segment, built from point, line, distance and arc, and explain why precise definitions are needed in proof
409.ev: Writes a precise definition of a circle
409.q: If {{name}} defines a circle as 'a round shape', can they improve the definition so it would work in a proof?

410.desc: Explain a proof of Pythagoras' theorem (for example by rearranging areas) and use the converse to test whether a triangle is right-angled
410.q: If {{name}} is given a triangle with sides 9, 12 and 15, can they decide whether it is right-angled and explain the logic?

411.desc: Write proofs that vertical angles are equal, that alternate and corresponding angles are equal when lines are parallel, and that points on a perpendicular bisector are equidistant from the endpoints
411.ev: Proves that vertically opposite angles are equal
411.q: If {{name}} is asked to prove that vertically opposite angles are always equal, can they write a proof that works for every case?

412.desc: Define rotations, reflections and translations precisely, and compare transformations that preserve distance and angle (rigid motions) with those that do not, such as enlargements and stretches
412.ev: Defines a rotation by centre and angle
412.q: If {{name}} compares a reflection with an enlargement, can they say which keeps lengths the same and why?

413.desc: Perform and describe sequences of transformations that map one figure onto another, find a single equivalent transformation, and show that order can matter
413.ev: Maps a shape onto another with a reflection then a translation
413.q: If {{name}} reflects a triangle in the y-axis then the x-axis, can they find a single transformation that does the same?

414.desc: Use formulae for the volume of pyramids and cones (⅓ × base area × height) and spheres (4/3 πr³) to solve problems, including composite solids
414.ev: Calculates the volume of a cone
414.q: If {{name}} has an ice-cream cone topped by a hemisphere, can they work out the total volume?

415.desc: Explain that sine, cosine and tangent are well defined because all right triangles with the same acute angle are similar, so their side ratios are equal
415.ev: Explains why the ratio opposite/hypotenuse is the same in similar triangles
415.q: If {{name}} draws two different-sized right triangles with a 35° angle, can they explain why the ratio of opposite to hypotenuse is the same?

417.desc: Prove that any two circles are similar by a translation and a dilation, and explain why this makes π the same ratio for every circle
417.ev: Describes transformations mapping one circle onto another
417.q: If {{name}} is asked why π is the same for a coin and for the Earth's equator, can they explain using similarity?

418.desc: Use the facts that if lengths scale by k then areas scale by k² and volumes by k³ to solve problems about similar shapes and solids
418.ev: Finds the area of an enlarged shape
418.q: If {{name}} has two similar jugs and one is twice as tall, can they work out how many times more it holds?

419.desc: Derive and use the formula area = ½ab sin C for any triangle, using two sides and the included angle
419.ev: Derives the formula from base × height
419.q: If {{name}} has a triangular field with sides 80 m and 65 m meeting at 70°, can they find its area?

422.desc: Decide whether a problem needs right-triangle trigonometry, Pythagoras, the sine rule or the cosine rule from the information given, and solve multi-step problems
422.ev: Explains which rule fits each set of given information
422.q: If {{name}} is given a surveying problem with two angles and a distance, can they choose the right rule and explain the choice?

423.desc: Use circle theorems about angles: the angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference, angles in the same segment are equal, the angle in a semicircle is 90°, and opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral sum to 180°
423.ev: Finds angles using the centre-circumference theorem
423.q: If {{name}} sees a triangle drawn in a semicircle, can they say what the angle opposite the diameter must be and why?

424.desc: Use theorems that a tangent is perpendicular to the radius, two tangents from a point are equal, the perpendicular from the centre bisects a chord, and the alternate segment theorem
424.ev: Finds an angle using tangent ⟂ radius
424.q: If {{name}} sees two tangents drawn from a point to a circle, can they explain why the tangents are the same length?

425.desc: Define two figures as congruent when a sequence of rigid motions maps one onto the other, and use this to decide congruence and identify corresponding parts
425.ev: Shows two triangles are congruent by describing rigid motions
425.q: If {{name}} is given two triangles on a grid, can they show they're congruent by describing a sequence of rigid motions?

426.desc: Identify the shapes of cross-sections of 3-D solids and the solids generated by rotating 2-D shapes about an axis
426.ev: Describes cross-sections of a cone at different angles
426.q: If {{name}} spins a right triangle about one of its shorter sides, can they name the solid it traces out?

427.desc: Derive and recall exact values of sin, cos and tan for 0°, 30°, 45°, 60° and 90° from special triangles, giving answers in surd form
427.ev: Derives sin 60° from an equilateral triangle
427.q: If {{name}} has no calculator, can they work out the exact value of cos 30° from a triangle?

429.desc: Carry out formal constructions (copy an angle, bisect segments and angles, perpendiculars, parallels, inscribed equilateral triangle, square and hexagon) and justify them with congruence
429.ev: Copies an angle with compass and straightedge
429.q: If {{name}} bisects an angle with compasses, can they explain using congruent triangles why the construction works?

430.desc: Sketch and interpret the graphs of y = sin x, y = cos x and y = tan x for angles in degrees, identifying period, amplitude, symmetries and asymptotes
430.ev: Sketches y = sin x from 0° to 360°
430.q: If {{name}} knows sin 30° = 0.5, can they use the graph to find another angle between 0° and 360° with the same sine?

432.desc: Model real objects with geometric solids to solve design problems, including density calculations such as mass from volume and population density from area
432.ev: Models a tree trunk as a cylinder to estimate its mass
432.q: If {{name}} models a log as a cylinder and knows the density of wood, can they estimate its mass?

433.desc: Verify that a dilation maps lines to parallel lines (or leaves lines through the centre unchanged) and multiplies all lengths by the scale factor
433.ev: Shows that a dilated segment is parallel to the original
433.q: If {{name}} dilates a triangle by scale factor 3 from a point outside it, can they say what happens to the side lengths and the directions of the sides?

435.desc: Prove that opposite sides and angles of a parallelogram are equal, that its diagonals bisect each other, and that a parallelogram with equal diagonals is a rectangle
435.ev: Proves opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal
435.q: If {{name}} is told a parallelogram's diagonals are equal, can they prove it must be a rectangle?

436.desc: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems, such as showing a quadrilateral is a parallelogram or rectangle, or a point lies on a circle
436.ev: Proves a quadrilateral is a parallelogram using gradients
436.q: If {{name}} is given four vertices, can they prove whether the shape is a rectangle?

437.desc: Prove theorems about triangles: interior angles sum to 180°, base angles of isosceles triangles are equal, the midpoint segment is parallel to the third side and half its length, and medians meet at a point
437.ev: Proves the angle sum of a triangle using parallel lines
437.q: If {{name}} is asked to prove that a triangle's angles add to 180°, can they do it using a parallel line?

438.desc: Find lengths and angles in 3-D shapes by identifying right-angled triangles, such as the space diagonal of a cuboid and the angle between a line and a plane
438.ev: Calculates the length of the diagonal of a cuboid
438.q: If {{name}} has a box 30 × 40 × 120 cm, can they work out whether a 1.3 m rod fits inside diagonally?

416.desc: Define figures as similar when a sequence of rigid motions and dilations maps one onto the other, and explain that similar triangles have equal angles and proportional sides
416.ev: Shows two figures are similar by describing transformations
416.q: If {{name}} is given two triangles of different sizes, can they show they're similar by describing transformations?

439.desc: Explain and use the relationship sin θ = cos(90° − θ) in right triangles
439.ev: Explains the relationship using one right triangle
439.q: If {{name}} is told sin x = cos 25°, can they find x and explain why?

440.desc: Calculate the curved surface area of cones (πrl) and spheres (4πr²), finding the slant height with Pythagoras when needed
440.ev: Calculates the surface area of a sphere
440.q: If {{name}} has a conical party hat of radius 8 cm and height 15 cm, can they find how much card it needs?

441.desc: Establish that two triangles with two pairs of equal angles are similar, and use the criterion to identify similar triangles in diagrams with parallel lines
441.ev: Explains why AA is enough to prove similarity
441.q: If {{name}} sees two triangles that share an angle and have parallel sides, can they explain why the triangles are similar?

421.desc: Prove and use the cosine rule a² = b² + c² − 2bc cos A to find a side from two sides and the included angle, or an angle from three sides
421.ev: Finds a side from two sides and the included angle
421.q: If {{name}} knows all three sides of a triangle, can they find the largest angle?

442.desc: Derive the equation of a circle with centre (a, b) and radius r from Pythagoras, and find centre and radius from equations, including by completing the square
442.ev: Writes the equation of a circle with given centre and radius
442.q: If {{name}} is given x² + y² − 6x + 4y − 3 = 0, can they find the centre and radius?

420.desc: Prove and use the sine rule a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C to find missing sides and angles in non-right-angled triangles
420.ev: Uses the sine rule to find a side
420.q: If {{name}} knows two angles and one side of a triangle, can they find another side?

428.desc: Explain why SSS, SAS, ASA and RHS guarantee congruence using rigid motions, and show with a counterexample why SSA does not
428.q: If {{name}} is told two triangles share two sides and a non-included angle, can they show the triangles might not be congruent?

434.desc: Prove that triangles are congruent using a named criterion, and use congruence to prove further facts such as equal lengths or angles
434.ev: Writes a congruence proof with reasons
434.q: If {{name}} is asked to prove that the diagonals of a kite cross at right angles, can they use congruent triangles to do it?

443.desc: Recognise the circle, ellipse, parabola and hyperbola as the curves made by slicing a double cone with a plane at different angles, and match each to its typical Cartesian equation
443.ev: Describes how the angle of the plane gives each conic
443.q: If {{name}} is shown a torch beam hitting a wall at different angles, can they name the conic formed each time?

445.desc: Convert between polar and Cartesian coordinates using x = r cos θ, y = r sin θ, r = √(x² + y²) and tan θ = y/x, choosing θ in the correct quadrant
445.q: If {{name}} is given the Cartesian point (−3, −3), can they find its polar coordinates with θ in the right quadrant?

446.desc: Find the equation of the tangent to a circle at a given point using the perpendicular gradient to the radius
446.ev: Finds the gradient of the radius
446.q: If {{name}} is given the circle x² + y² = 25 and the point (3, 4), can they find the equation of the tangent there?

448.desc: Identify the vertex, focus, directrix and axis of parabolas such as y² = 4ax, x² = 4ay and translated forms (y − k)² = 4a(x − h)
448.ev: States the focus and directrix of y² = 12x
448.q: If {{name}} is given (y + 3)² = −8(x − 1), can they find the vertex, focus and directrix and sketch the curve?

449.desc: Construct the incircle and circumcircle of a triangle using angle bisectors and perpendicular bisectors, and prove properties of a cyclic quadrilateral
449.ev: Constructs the circumcircle of a triangle
449.q: If {{name}} needs a circle that passes through three villages, can they construct it and explain why it works?

451.desc: Choose and fit trigonometric functions of the form y = A sin(B(x − C)) + D to periodic data such as tides, daylight hours or a Ferris wheel, interpreting amplitude, period and midline
451.ev: Identifies amplitude, period and midline from data
451.q: If {{name}} has tide heights that rise and fall every 12.4 hours, can they write a sine model and use it to predict the height at a given time?

444.desc: Locate points with polar coordinates (r, θ), using a pole and an initial line with θ measured anticlockwise in radians, and recognise that a point has many polar representations
444.ev: Plots points given in polar coordinates
444.q: If {{name}} is given the point (3, 2π/3) in polar coordinates, can they plot it and give another pair of polar coordinates for the same point?

453.desc: Prove circle theorems, such as the angle at the centre theorem and the angle in a semicircle, using isosceles triangles formed by radii
453.ev: Proves the angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference
453.q: If {{name}} joins the centre to a point on the circle, can they use the isosceles triangles to prove the angle in a semicircle is a right angle?

454.desc: Prove theorems using similar triangles, such as the side-splitter theorem and a proof of Pythagoras' theorem from the altitude to the hypotenuse
454.ev: Proves that a line parallel to one side divides the others proportionally
454.q: If {{name}} draws the altitude to the hypotenuse of a right triangle, can they use similar triangles to prove Pythagoras' theorem?

450.desc: Define a radian as the angle subtended by an arc equal in length to the radius, convert between degrees and radians, and use radians in arc length s = rθ
450.ev: Explains why 2π radians make a full turn
450.q: If {{name}} wraps a piece of string the length of a radius round a circle, can they explain what angle it makes at the centre?

455.desc: Solve equations such as 2 sin x = 1 or cos 2x = 0.3 in a given interval, using inverse trig functions and symmetry to find every solution
455.ev: Finds all solutions of sin x = 0.5 in 0 ≤ x < 2π
455.q: If {{name}} solves sin x = 0.5 and gets 30°, can they find all the other solutions between 0° and 360°?

165.desc: Use the unit circle to explain that sine and cosine are periodic with period 2π, that cosine is even and sine is odd, and identities such as sin(π − θ) = sin θ
165.q: If {{name}} knows sin(π/6) = ½, can they use symmetry to find sin(5π/6) and explain why?

189.desc: Prove sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 from the unit circle and Pythagoras, and use it to find one ratio from another and the quadrant
189.q: If {{name}} knows sin θ = 3/5 and θ is obtuse, can they find cos θ?

447.desc: Derive the equation of a parabola as the locus of points equidistant from a focus and a directrix, for example y² = 4ax from the focus (a, 0) and the directrix x = −a, or y = x²/(4p) from (0, p) and y = −p
447.ev: Writes the distances to the focus and directrix algebraically
447.q: If {{name}} is given the focus (0, 2) and the directrix y = −2, can they derive the equation of the parabola?

182.desc: Use the unit circle to define sine and cosine for any angle as the coordinates of a point on the circle, explaining signs in each quadrant
182.ev: Finds sin and cos of 150° from the unit circle
182.q: If {{name}} sees a point on the unit circle at 210°, can they say what its coordinates tell them about sin 210° and cos 210°?

458.desc: Find a unit vector in the direction of a given vector, and decide whether vectors are parallel by checking whether one is a scalar multiple of the other
458.ev: Finds the unit vector in the direction of (2, −1, 2)
458.q: If {{name}} is given the vectors (3, −6, 9) and (−1, 2, k), can they find k so that the vectors are parallel?

457.desc: Use vector algebra to prove geometric results such as points being collinear or lines being parallel
457.ev: Expresses a path in terms of given vectors
457.q: If {{name}} is given a parallelogram described with vectors a and b, can they prove the diagonals bisect each other?

456.desc: Represent vectors in three dimensions as column vectors and with i, j, k notation, find the vector between two points from their position vectors, and calculate magnitudes with √(x² + y² + z²)
456.ev: Writes a vector in both column and i, j, k form
456.q: If {{name}} has the points A(1, 2, −1) and B(4, 0, 5), can they find the vector from A to B and its length?

461.desc: Give informal arguments for formulae for circumference, circle area, and volumes of cylinders, pyramids, cones and spheres using dissection and Cavalieri's principle
461.ev: Explains why a cone is one-third of a cylinder
461.q: If {{name}} stacks coins straight and then slanted, can they explain why the volume is the same using Cavalieri's principle?

464.desc: Find the acute angle between two lines using the scalar product of their direction vectors
464.ev: Finds the angle between two intersecting lines
464.q: If {{name}} has two lines in vector form, can they find the acute angle between them?

463.desc: Find the angle between two vectors using cos θ = a·b/(|a||b|), including angles in 3-D shapes
463.ev: Finds the angle between two 3-D vectors
463.q: If {{name}} has the vertices of a triangle in 3-D, can they find one of its angles using vectors?

196.desc: Prove and use the addition formulae for sin(A ± B), cos(A ± B) and tan(A ± B), and derive the double-angle formulae, including cos 2A = 2cos²A − 1 = 1 − 2sin²A
196.ev: Uses sin(A + B) to find the exact value of sin 75°
196.q: If {{name}} needs the exact value of cos 15°, can they find it using a compound-angle formula?

469.desc: Use conics to model real situations: planetary orbits as ellipses with the Sun at a focus, comet paths, reflectors and hyperbolic navigation, judging which conic and parameters fit
469.ev: Describes a planetary orbit using eccentricity
469.q: If {{name}} is given the eccentricity and major axis of Earth's orbit, can they find its closest and furthest distances from the Sun?

471.desc: Use the polar equation r = l/(1 + e cos θ), with a focus at the pole, to describe ellipses, parabolas and hyperbolas, and relate l and e to the shape
471.ev: Identifies the conic from a polar equation
471.q: If {{name}} is given r = 8/(1 + 0.5 cos θ), can they identify the conic and find its closest distance to the pole?

470.desc: Convert curve equations between polar and Cartesian form using r² = x² + y², x = r cos θ and y = r sin θ, recognising circles and lines in either form
470.ev: Shows that r = 4 cos θ is a circle and finds its centre and radius
470.q: If {{name}} is given the polar equation r = 6 sin θ, can they find its Cartesian equation and describe the curve?

466.desc: Define every conic as the locus where the distance to a focus is e times the distance to a directrix, with e < 1 for an ellipse, e = 1 for a parabola and e > 1 for a hyperbola, and find foci and directrices x = ±a/e
466.ev: Calculates the eccentricity of an ellipse and a hyperbola
466.q: If {{name}} is given the ellipse x²/25 + y²/16 = 1, can they find its eccentricity, foci and directrices?

475.desc: Write the equation of a plane in the forms r·n = a·n, ax + by + cz = d and r = a + sb + tc, and identify a normal vector
475.ev: Finds the Cartesian equation of a plane from a point and a normal
475.q: If {{name}} has three points that are not on one line, can they find the Cartesian equation of the plane through them?

477.desc: Investigate how parameters change families of polar curves, such as limaçons r = a + b cos θ (with a dimple, cusp or inner loop) and roses r = a sin nθ (n petals for odd n, 2n petals for even n)
477.ev: Describes how r = a + b cos θ changes as a/b changes
477.q: If {{name}} is exploring r = a + 2 cos θ, can they describe how the shape changes as a increases from 1 to 5?

479.desc: Use the parametric form to show that the endpoints of a focal chord of y² = 4ax have parameters with pq = −1, and find the length of the latus rectum (4a)
479.ev: Shows that pq = −1 for a focal chord
479.q: If {{name}} knows one end of a focal chord of y² = 8x is at (2, 4), can they find the other end?

473.desc: Use the fact that the difference of the distances from any point on a hyperbola to the two foci is constant (2a) to derive its equation, and locate the foci using b² = c² − a²
473.ev: Finds the foci of x²/9 − y²/16 = 1
473.q: If {{name}} is told the foci of a hyperbola are (±5, 0) and the difference of distances is 6, can they find its equation?

472.desc: Use the fact that the sum of the distances from any point on an ellipse to the two foci is constant (2a) to derive its equation, and locate the foci using b² = a² − c²
472.ev: Finds the foci of x²/25 + y²/16 = 1
472.q: If {{name}} is told the foci of an ellipse are (±4, 0) and the sum of distances is 10, can they find its equation?

482.desc: Use a Cartesian graph of r against θ to see where r is greatest, smallest and zero, and so to sketch the corresponding polar curve
482.ev: Draws the graph of r = 2 + cos θ against θ
482.q: If {{name}} has a graph of r against θ, can they use it to sketch the polar curve?

483.desc: Decide whether two lines in 3-D are parallel, intersect or are skew by comparing direction vectors and solving for the parameters, and find any point of intersection
483.ev: Finds the point where two lines meet
483.q: If {{name}} is given two lines in vector form, can they show whether they intersect, are parallel or are skew?

484.desc: Find where a line meets a conic by substitution, and use the discriminant to find conditions for a line to be a tangent, such as c = a/m for y = mx + c and y² = 4ax
484.ev: Finds the intersections of a line and an ellipse
484.q: If {{name}} has the line y = mx + 2 and the ellipse x² + 4y² = 8, can they find the values of m for which the line is a tangent?

486.desc: Find the line of intersection of two planes and the angle between two planes using their normals
486.ev: Finds the line of intersection of two planes
486.q: If {{name}} has two plane equations, can they find their line of intersection and the angle between the planes?

488.desc: Find where two polar curves meet by solving r₁(θ) = r₂(θ), checking the pole separately because it can be reached at different values of θ
488.ev: Finds the intersections of r = 1 + cos θ and r = 3 cos θ
488.q: If {{name}} has a cardioid and a circle in polar form, can they find all their points of intersection?

490.desc: Find the locus of a point defined using a conic, such as the midpoint of a chord or the intersection of two tangents, by writing it in terms of a parameter and eliminating the parameter
490.ev: Finds the locus of midpoints of chords of a parabola
490.q: If {{name}} considers the midpoints of all chords of y² = 4x through the origin, can they find the locus of the midpoints?

492.desc: Choose polar coordinates for contexts with a natural centre, such as radar, navigation, spiral growth or the paths of points on rotating objects, and explain when polar form is simpler than Cartesian
492.ev: Describes a radar position in polar coordinates
492.q: If {{name}} is describing the position of ships on a radar screen, can they explain why polar coordinates are a natural choice?

478.desc: Use parametric forms of the conics: (at², 2at) for y² = 4ax, (a cos θ, b sin θ) for an ellipse, (a cosh t, b sinh t) or (a sec θ, b tan θ) for a hyperbola, and (ct, c/t) for xy = c²
478.ev: Verifies that a parametric point satisfies the Cartesian equation
478.q: If {{name}} is given x = 3 cos θ, y = 2 sin θ, can they show the curve is an ellipse and find its Cartesian equation?

493.desc: Treat a polar curve r = f(θ) as the parametric curve x = f(θ)cos θ, y = f(θ)sin θ with parameter θ
493.ev: Writes a polar curve in parametric form
493.q: If {{name}} is given r = 1 + cos θ, can they write parametric equations for x and y in terms of θ?

494.desc: Identify a conic from an equation such as 4x² + 9y² − 16x + 18y = 11 by completing the square, and find its centre, axes and foci
494.ev: Completes the square in x and y
494.q: If {{name}} is given 9x² − 4y² − 36x − 8y = 4, can they identify the conic and find its centre?

467.desc: Explain the reflective properties of conics: rays parallel to the axis of a parabola reflect through the focus, and rays from one focus of an ellipse reflect through the other
467.ev: Explains why a satellite dish is parabolic
467.q: If {{name}} is asked why a car headlight has a parabolic mirror with the bulb at the focus, can they explain?

497.desc: Find the shortest distance from a point to a line and from a point to a plane, using perpendicularity and the scalar product
497.ev: Finds the foot of the perpendicular from a point to a line
497.q: If {{name}} has a point and a plane, can they find how far the point is from the plane?

476.desc: Sketch polar curves by finding where r is greatest, smallest and zero, using symmetry and tangents at the pole, and keeping to r ≥ 0 when that convention is used
476.ev: Finds the values of θ where r = 0
476.q: If {{name}} is given r = 3 cos 2θ, can they sketch the curve and show where it passes through the pole?

487.desc: Solve trigonometric equations such as sin 2θ = sin θ or cos 2θ = cos θ by rewriting with double-angle formulae and factorising, finding all solutions in a given interval
487.ev: Rewrites sin 2θ as 2 sin θ cos θ and factorises
487.q: If {{name}} needs to solve sin 2θ = cos θ for 0 ≤ θ < 2π, can they find every solution?

491.desc: Recognise and sketch standard polar curves: circles r = a and r = 2a cos θ, half-lines θ = α, spirals r = aθ, cardioids r = a(1 + cos θ) and roses r = a sin nθ
491.q: If {{name}} is shown four polar curves, can they match each to its equation and explain their choice?

498.desc: Use symmetry to sketch polar curves and simplify calculations: if replacing θ by −θ leaves r unchanged, the curve is symmetric about the initial line
498.ev: Tests a polar curve for symmetry in the initial line
498.q: If {{name}} is given r = 2 + 3 cos θ, can they explain why the curve is symmetric about the initial line?

489.desc: Find equations of tangents and normals to conics using implicit or parametric differentiation, including standard results such as the tangent ty = x + at² to y² = 4ax
489.ev: Finds the tangent to an ellipse at a given point
489.q: If {{name}} is given the point (2 cos θ, sin θ) on an ellipse, can they find the equation of the tangent there?

481.desc: Sketch the ellipse x²/a² + y²/b² = 1, identify its intercepts and major and minor axes, and see it as a circle stretched in one direction
481.ev: Sketches an ellipse from its equation
481.q: If {{name}} is given x²/25 + y²/9 = 1, can they sketch the ellipse and mark its intercepts?

480.desc: Sketch the hyperbola x²/a² − y²/b² = 1 with its two branches, vertices and asymptotes y = ±(b/a)x
480.ev: Sketches a hyperbola from its equation
480.q: If {{name}} is given x²/16 − y²/9 = 1, can they sketch the hyperbola with its asymptotes?

502.desc: Recognise xy = c² as a hyperbola with perpendicular asymptotes (the coordinate axes), use the parametric form (ct, c/t), and link it to y = k/x
502.ev: Sketches xy = 16 and states its asymptotes
502.q: If {{name}} is given xy = 9, can they explain why it is a hyperbola and give a parametric form?

465.desc: Calculate the scalar product a·b = a₁b₁ + a₂b₂ + a₃b₃ = |a||b|cos θ, and use a·b = 0 to test whether vectors are perpendicular
465.ev: Calculates a scalar product from components
465.q: If {{name}} is given the vectors (2, −1, 3) and (1, 5, 1), can they decide whether the vectors are perpendicular?

474.desc: Calculate the vector product a × b, a vector perpendicular to both a and b with magnitude |a||b|sin θ, and use it to find normals and areas
474.ev: Calculates a × b using the determinant layout
474.q: If {{name}} has two direction vectors in a plane, can they find a vector perpendicular to both?

505.desc: Apply translations, stretches, reflections and rotations through 90° to conics and find the transformed equations, including using matrices
505.ev: Finds the equation after a translation by a vector
505.q: If {{name}} translates y² = 8x by the vector (3, −1), can they write the new equation and state the new focus?

462.desc: Write the equation of a line as r = a + tb in two or three dimensions, interpret a and b, and convert between vector, parametric and Cartesian forms
462.ev: Writes the vector equation of the line through two points
462.q: If {{name}} is given the points (1, 0, 2) and (3, 4, −1), can they write a vector equation of the line through them and check whether (5, 8, −4) lies on it?

496.desc: Find the point where a line meets a plane, decide whether a line is parallel to or lies in a plane, and find the angle between a line and a plane
496.ev: Finds the point of intersection of a line and a plane
496.q: If {{name}} has a line and a plane, can they find where the line crosses the plane and the angle between them?

probes.q: If {{name}} rolls a die 60 times and records the results, can they compare how often each number came up with what they'd expect in theory — and explain why they might not match perfectly?
If {{name}} flips a coin and rolls a dice, can they find the probability of a head and a six and explain why they multiply?
If {{name}} guesses every answer on a 10-question multiple-choice test with 4 options, can they find the probability of getting exactly 5 right?

532.desc: Describe, interpret, and compare distributions of a single variable using appropriate measures of central tendency (mean, median, mode) and spread (range), including the effect of outliers
532.ev: Calculate mean, median, and mode for a data set and explain when each is most appropriate
532.q: If {{name}} had the test scores of a whole class, could they find the mean, median, and range, and explain what each tells you about how the class performed?

535.desc: Understand and apply the rule that probabilities of all mutually exclusive outcomes sum to one; use this to find the probability of a complementary event (P(not A) = 1 − P(A))
535.ev: Verify that probabilities of all outcomes listed for a spinner sum to 1
535.q: If a spinner has three sections and one has a probability of 0.4 and another has 0.35, can {{name}} work out the probability of landing on the third section without being told?

537.desc: Display numerical data on dot plots and equal-width histograms, and read off features such as clusters, gaps and peaks
537.ev: Draws a dot plot of a small data set
537.q: If {{name}} has the times 25 students took to run a lap, can they draw a histogram and describe what it shows?

539.desc: Record, describe, and analyse the frequency of outcomes from probability experiments to develop an understanding of relative frequency as an estimate of probability
539.ev: Conduct a coin-toss experiment, record results in a frequency table, and calculate relative frequencies
539.q: If {{name}} rolls a die 60 times and records the results, can they compare how often each number came up with what they'd expect in theory — and explain why they might not match perfectly?

541.desc: Calculate and interpret the mean absolute deviation as the average distance of data values from the mean
541.ev: Calculates the MAD of a small data set
541.q: If {{name}} compares two basketball players' points per game, can they use the MAD to say whose scoring is more consistent?

530.desc: Construct and interpret frequency tables, bar charts, pie charts, pictograms, and vertical line charts for both categorical and grouped numerical data, choosing appropriate representations for the data type
530.ev: Construct a grouped frequency table from raw continuous data, choosing appropriate class intervals
530.q: When {{name}} collects data for a project, can they choose the right type of chart to display it — and draw it accurately with correct labels and a suitable scale?

544.desc: Recognise a statistical question as one that expects variability in the answers (e.g. 'How tall are students in my class?') and understand that a data set has a distribution described by centre, spread and shape
544.ev: Sorts questions into statistical and non-statistical
544.q: If {{name}} is given 'How many pets does each student have?' and 'How many pets do I have?', can they say which is statistical and why?

534.desc: Understand probability as a measure on a scale from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain); use the language of probability including likely, unlikely, certain, and impossible
534.ev: Place everyday events on a 0-to-1 probability scale with justification
534.q: Can {{name}} explain that probability goes from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain), place events on that scale as numbers, and tell you whether a game is fair or not?

536.desc: Classify data as categorical or numerical, and numerical data as discrete or continuous, and choose suitable displays for each type
536.ev: Classifies shoe size, height and eye colour
536.q: If {{name}} collects favourite sports, number of siblings and reaction times, can they classify each type of data?

546.desc: Calculate the mean, median and mode from ungrouped frequency tables
546.ev: Calculates the mean from a frequency table
546.q: If {{name}} has a table of how many goals were scored in 30 matches, can they find the mean number of goals?

547.desc: Choose the most appropriate average for a data set and context, explaining how outliers and skew affect the mean more than the median
547.ev: Explains why median is better for house prices
547.q: If {{name}} sees that one employee earns £1 million, can they explain why the median salary is more useful than the mean?

549.desc: Design and use simulations with random number generators, coins or spreadsheets to estimate probabilities of compound events
549.ev: Designs a simulation for a real situation
549.q: If {{name}} wants to estimate the chance that a family of four children has at least three girls, can they design a coin simulation?

550.desc: Calculate the expected number of times an outcome will occur as probability × number of trials, and compare expected with observed results
550.q: If {{name}} rolls a dice 120 times, can they work out how many 4s to expect and explain why they probably won't get exactly that?

551.desc: Distinguish a population from a sample, explain why samples are used, and understand that a sample is only valid for a population if it is representative
551.ev: Identifies the population and sample in a study
551.q: If {{name}} surveys 50 students to find out about the whole school, can they name the population and sample and explain one risk?

552.desc: Enumerate sets and their unions and intersections systematically using tables, grids, and Venn diagrams to organise and count outcomes
552.ev: List the elements in the union and intersection of two sets using a Venn diagram
552.q: Can {{name}} use a table or Venn diagram to systematically list all the possible outcomes of two events — like rolling two dice — and use it to count favourable outcomes?

548.desc: Generate theoretical sample spaces for single and combined events using listing, tables, and tree diagrams, and calculate theoretical probabilities as the number of favourable outcomes divided by the total number of equally likely outcomes
548.ev: List all 36 outcomes when rolling two dice and find P(total = 7)
548.q: Can {{name}} draw a tree diagram to map out all possible outcomes of a two-step probability situation — like flipping a coin and then rolling a die — and calculate the probability of any particular combination?

553.desc: Construct and interpret Venn diagrams with two or three sets to organise and count outcomes; use systematic listing and the product rule for counting to enumerate all possible outcomes of combined events
553.ev: Draw a two-circle Venn diagram to sort 30 students by whether they like football, like cricket, or like both
553.q: If {{name}} surveys a class about which sports they play and draws a Venn diagram to show the results, can they use it to find out how many students play both sports — and calculate the probability of picking one of those students at random?

554.desc: Identify sources of bias such as convenience samples, voluntary response, leading questions and non-response, and suggest improvements
554.ev: Explains why surveying a gym about exercise habits is biased
554.q: If {{name}} sees a survey of shoppers at 10 am on a weekday, can they explain who is left out and how that could bias results?

556.desc: Draw and interpret box plots from the five-number summary, reading off median, quartiles and range
556.ev: Draws a box plot from a five-number summary
556.q: If {{name}} is shown a box plot of reaction times, can they read off the median and the IQR?

559.desc: Plan a data collection: write clear unbiased questions with suitable response options, choose a sampling method, and pilot the questionnaire
559.ev: Writes a question with non-overlapping response boxes
559.q: If {{name}} wants to find out how much screen time students have, can they design a good question and a fair sampling plan?

560.desc: Estimate the mean from grouped frequency tables using midpoints, identify the modal class and the class containing the median, and explain why the mean is an estimate
560.ev: Uses midpoints to estimate the mean
560.q: If {{name}} has heights grouped in 10 cm classes, can they estimate the mean height and explain why it's not exact?

561.desc: Use data from a random sample to estimate population characteristics, such as scaling a sample proportion up to a population
561.ev: Estimates the number in a population from a sample proportion
561.q: If {{name}} finds that 12 of 50 sampled students walk to school, can they estimate how many of the 900 students do?

562.desc: Identify mutually exclusive events and use P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) for them, recognising when events are not mutually exclusive
562.ev: Decides whether two events are mutually exclusive
562.q: If {{name}} picks a card, can they explain why P(king or heart) isn't simply P(king) + P(heart)?

555.desc: Find the lower quartile, median, upper quartile and interquartile range of a data set, and explain why IQR is resistant to outliers
555.ev: Finds the quartiles of an ordered list
555.q: If {{name}} has a list of 11 test scores, can they find the quartiles and the IQR?

557.desc: Describe and carry out simple random, systematic and stratified sampling, and explain why random selection helps produce representative samples
557.ev: Describes how to choose a simple random sample
557.q: If {{name}} needs a sample of 40 from a school of 800 with different year sizes, can they work out a stratified sample?

563.desc: Plot bivariate data on a scatter graph with correctly labelled axes and appropriate scales; describe the correlation (positive, negative, none) and draw an estimated line of best fit where appropriate
563.ev: Plot 10 data points on a scatter graph with correct axis labels and a consistent scale
563.q: If {{name}} has data comparing hours of sleep and test scores for 10 students, can they plot the points on a scatter graph, draw a line of best fit, and use it to predict a score for someone who slept 7 hours?

86.desc: Describe simple mathematical relationships between two variables using scatter graphs, identify positive, negative, or no correlation, and use a line of best fit to make predictions
86.ev: Plot bivariate data on a scatter graph and describe the type of correlation observed
86.q: If {{name}} plotted a scatter graph — say, comparing hours of revision and test scores — could they draw a line of best fit, describe the pattern, and use it to make a prediction?

564.desc: Identify ways graphs and statistics mislead — truncated axes, unequal intervals, 3-D effects, cherry-picked data, inappropriate averages — and redraw a fair version
564.q: If {{name}} sees an advert graph where one bar looks twice as tall but the axis starts at 90, can they explain why it's misleading?

566.desc: Use the product rule to count outcomes, such as the number of possible codes or outfits
566.q: If {{name}} has 3 starters, 4 mains and 2 desserts on a menu, can they work out how many different meals are possible?

567.desc: Plot and interpret time series graphs, describing trends and seasonal patterns and making cautious predictions
567.q: If {{name}} sees monthly ice-cream sales over three years, can they describe the trend and the seasonal pattern?

568.desc: Construct and interpret two-way tables of categorical data, calculating joint, marginal and conditional relative frequencies to look for associations
568.ev: Completes a two-way table from information
568.q: If {{name}} has survey data on age group and favourite music, can they build a two-way table and see if the two are linked?

569.desc: Use the capture–recapture method to estimate the size of an animal population, stating the assumptions it relies on
569.ev: Calculates a population estimate from capture data
569.q: If {{name}} marks 40 fish, then catches 50 later of which 8 are marked, can they estimate the number of fish in the lake?

570.desc: Compare two distributions using box plots, commenting on centre (median) and spread (IQR) in context
570.ev: Writes a comparison of medians in context
570.q: If {{name}} sees box plots for two classes' test scores, can they write two sentences comparing them in context?

571.desc: Draw cumulative frequency graphs from grouped data and use them to estimate the median, quartiles and the number above or below a value
571.ev: Plots cumulative frequency at upper class boundaries
571.q: If {{name}} has grouped data on journey times, can they draw a cumulative frequency graph and estimate the median?

572.desc: Describe events as subsets of a sample space using unions, intersections and complements, with set notation
572.ev: Lists the sample space and identifies an event
572.q: If {{name}} rolls a dice, can they describe the event 'even and greater than 3' using set notation?

573.desc: Explain what it means for events to be independent and use P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B) for independent events, including on tree diagrams
573.ev: Decides whether two events are independent
573.q: If {{name}} flips a coin and rolls a dice, can they find the probability of a head and a six and explain why they multiply?

574.desc: Explain that different random samples give different results, that this variation shrinks as sample size grows, and generate multiple samples to see it
574.ev: Simulates several samples and compares their means
574.q: If {{name}} takes ten samples of 5 and ten samples of 50, can they predict which set of sample means will vary more?

575.desc: Describe distributions as symmetric, positively or negatively skewed, or bimodal, and explain how shape affects the relative positions of mean and median
575.q: If {{name}} sees a histogram of incomes with a long tail to the right, can they say which is bigger, the mean or the median, and why?

576.desc: Find conditional probabilities from two-way tables and Venn diagrams by restricting to the given condition
576.ev: Finds P(A given B) from a two-way table
576.q: If {{name}} has a table of students by year and lunch choice, can they find the probability a Year 9 student chose pasta?

577.desc: Draw and interpret histograms with unequal class widths using frequency density = frequency ÷ class width, and estimate frequencies from areas
577.q: If {{name}} has a histogram with bars of different widths, can they explain why the tallest bar may not have the most data?

578.desc: Use the 1.5 × IQR rule to identify outliers, show them on box plots, and decide whether to keep or remove them in context
578.q: If {{name}} finds a reaction time of 3.2 s among values near 0.3 s, can they test whether it's an outlier and decide what to do with it?

579.desc: Interpret the correlation coefficient r as a measure of the strength and direction of a linear association between −1 and 1, recognising that r can be near zero for a strong nonlinear pattern and is affected by outliers
579.ev: Matches scatter plots to values of r
579.q: If {{name}} is told the correlation between hours of revision and score is 0.85, can they explain what that does and does not show?

580.desc: Calculate (with technology) and interpret the standard deviation as a typical distance from the mean, and compare it with IQR and MAD
580.ev: Calculates standard deviation with a calculator
580.q: If {{name}} compares the daily temperatures of two cities with the same mean, can they use standard deviation to say which is more variable?

581.desc: Distinguish sample surveys, observational studies and randomised experiments, and explain that only randomised experiments can establish cause and effect
581.q: If {{name}} reads that coffee drinkers live longer, can they explain what kind of study that probably was and what it can't show?

582.desc: Use P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A and B) and interpret the answer in context
582.ev: Calculates P(A or B) for overlapping events
582.q: If {{name}} knows 60% of students play sport, 40% play music and 25% do both, can they find the percentage who do at least one?

583.desc: Use tree diagrams for events without replacement, where probabilities on second branches depend on the first outcome, and apply the general multiplication rule
583.ev: Draws a tree for picking two sweets without replacement
583.q: If {{name}} takes two socks from a drawer without looking, can they find the probability that both are black?

585.desc: Explain why a binomial critical region usually has a probability below the nominal significance level, and calculate this actual significance level
585.ev: Calculates the probability of the critical region under H₀
585.q: If {{name}} finds a critical region of X ≥ 9, can they calculate its actual significance level and explain why it isn't exactly 5%?

587.desc: Calculate P(X = r) = ⁿCᵣ pʳ(1 − p)ⁿ⁻ʳ, explaining where each factor comes from, and use technology for binomial probabilities
587.ev: Explains why the ⁿCᵣ factor is needed
587.q: If {{name}} guesses every answer on a 10-question multiple-choice test with 4 options, can they find the probability of getting exactly 5 right?

589.desc: Scale the Poisson parameter in proportion to the length of the interval, for example from 3 per hour to 1.5 per half-hour or 72 per day
589.ev: Rescales λ for a different time interval
589.q: If {{name}} knows faults occur at 0.8 per metre of cable, can they find the probability of no faults in a 5-metre length?

590.desc: Use data from a randomised experiment to compare two treatments, using simulation to decide whether a difference is larger than chance would produce
590.ev: Calculates the difference in means between groups
590.q: If {{name}} finds a new fertiliser group grew 3 cm taller on average, can they use simulation to judge whether that could be chance?

591.desc: Use P(A | B) = P(A and B) ÷ P(B), and test independence by checking whether P(A | B) = P(A)
591.ev: Calculates a conditional probability with the formula
